stories.headline: Amazon adds $17.5B Citigroup-led loan days after record C$14B Canadian bond sale

key_facts.fact: Amazon disclosed in a June 10 regulatory filing a $17.5B delayed-draw term loan from a group of banks led by Citigroup, with funds available through end-September and each draw repayable within three years.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon secured a $17.5 billion delayed draw term loan led by Citigroup, disclosed in a regulatory filing on June 10... The lenders have agreed to make the delayed draw term loan available until the end of September... Every time the company borrows money under this facility, it has three years from the date of the borrowing to repay it.

key_facts.fact: Syndicate members include JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, HSBC and Wells Fargo, with more than a dozen additional banks; pricing is SOFR plus 0.625-0.875 percentage points depending on Amazon's credit rating.
key_facts.excerpt: Other banks involved in the deal include JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America Corp., HSBC, and Wells Fargo & Co. More than a dozen additional banks contributed to the financing... The loan will pay 0.625 percentage point to 0.875 percentage point more than the Secured Overnight Financing Rate, or SOFR.

key_facts.fact: The loan comes two days after Amazon sold C$14B (~$10B) in Canadian-dollar bonds, the largest corporate bond sale on record in that currency; combined new financing in 48 hours is roughly $31.5B.
key_facts.excerpt: The loan comes just two days after it was reported that Amazon would also raise $14 billion in a Canadian bond sale, bringing its total new financing to roughly $31.5 billion in the span of roughly 48 hours.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's total short- and long-term debt (including lease payments) topped $225B as of March 31, up from roughly $150B a year earlier — a ~50% rise in 12 months — and the company has guided to about $200B in 2026 capex, mainly for data centers and chips.
key_facts.excerpt: As of 31 March, Amazon's total short- and long-term debt, including lease payments, exceeded $225 billion. A year earlier, that figure was closer to $150 billion... The company has said it plans to spend approximately $200 billion in capital expenditure in 2026, mainly on new data centres and chips. Q1 spending alone hit $43.2 billion.

stories.headline: Anthropic walks back covert Fable 5 limits on rival-AI work, makes safeguards visible

key_facts.fact: Anthropic reversed a policy that secretly degraded or refused Claude Fable 5 requests aimed at building competing AI models after backlash from researchers.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic is backtracking on a policy that would have covertly limited competitors from using its new AI model, Claude Fable 5, to develop other AI models. The company changed course after the move received significant backlash from the AI research community.

key_facts.fact: Starting this week flagged requests will visibly fall back to Opus 4.8, and API calls will return an explicit refusal reason every time it happens, Anthropic said.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting this week, flagged requests will visibly fall back to Opus 4.8. On the API, any flagged requests will return a reason for their refusal. You will see this every time it happens.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic apologized for the original hidden setup, saying it 'made the wrong tradeoff' on the visibility-versus-narrowness call.
key_facts.excerpt: We're changing Fable 5's safeguards for frontier LLM development to make them visible, the company said in a statement. We made the wrong tradeoff and we apologize for not getting the balance right.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic says the classifier currently triggers on roughly 0.05% of tasks and affects fewer than 0.05% of organizations, but a visible safeguard will have to flag more requests to remain robust.
key_facts.excerpt: Current usage shows that the classifier triggers on about 0.05% of tasks, affecting less than 0.05% of organizations. A visible safeguard needs to cast a wider net to be more robust, resulting in more requests being incorrectly flagged.

key_facts.fact: Cybersecurity researchers say Fable 5's guardrails reject innocuous tasks such as reading a blog post or running a code review, pushing many users back to Opus 4.8.
key_facts.excerpt: Fable seems totally unusable currently due to the over zealous rejection classifier, even for non related to cyber security. It rejects any request that could be tangentially cyber related. Even innocuous tasks like reading a blog post.

stories.headline: Anthropic publishes AI policy framework, pledges $350M for evaluations and fellowship

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released two policy proposals on June 10: an Advanced AI Framework for governing frontier models and an Economic Policy Framework for managing labor-market disruption.
key_facts.excerpt: We are sharing two policy proposals to prepare for AI progress. The first, our Advanced AI Framework, offers a roadmap for governing increasingly capable systems, from transparency and independent evaluation to government authority to block or deter dangerous deployments. The second, our Economic Policy Framework, turns to the question of how to prepare workers and the economy for AI's impact and ensure the financial benefits of AI are broadly shared.

key_facts.fact: The framework would give a regulator authority to block or deter deployment of models that pose a significant risk of catastrophic harm, with safeguards to prevent misuse of that power.
key_facts.excerpt: Enforcement and regulatory authority [should] be able to block or deter the deployment of models that pose a significant risk of catastrophic harm. We [are not proposing] heavy-handed regulatory power. Our [framework includes] a mechanism for blocking dangerous deployments, [with] concrete safeguards that would prevent that power from being misused.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic committed $200 million to a new Economic Futures Research Fund to back research trials and program evaluation on public policies for AI's labor impact.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said it will go to what it calls an Economic Futures Research Fund that will back research trials and 'program evaluation' on public policies it deems promising.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic is also funding a $150 million national fellowship program for early-career professionals to 'extend the benefits of AI to communities across America.'
key_facts.excerpt: The company is committing $350 million in total for two programs to help: $150 million to a national fellowship program for early-career people to 'extend the benefits of AI to communities across America,' and $200 million to its Economic Futures Research Fund.

key_facts.fact: The Economic Policy Framework proposes responses keyed to three scenarios: U.S. unemployment hitting 5%, 10%, and an unspecified 'unprecedented' level; in the worst case it floats universal basic income, sovereign wealth models, and equity-sharing.
key_facts.excerpt: The economic policy framework Anthropic proposed Wednesday set recommendations for how the U.S. government could respond to three levels of economic disruption caused by AI: one in which the national unemployment rate reaches 5%, 10% and an unspecified, 'unprecedented' level. In the 'unprecedented' scenario, the company wrote that more permanent support will be necessary, and it listed several ways to generate and share revenue broadly, including basic income, sovereign wealth models and equity-sharing mechanisms.

key_facts.fact: CEO Dario Amodei published a companion essay 'Policy on the AI Exponential' arguing policy is no longer fast enough for AI's pace, and proposing mandatory third-party testing for cyber, bio, and autonomy risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Alongside new policy proposals from the maker of the Claude chatbot, Anthropic CEO and co-founder Dario Amodei published an essay on his personal website that expanded on his position that the government should promise economic support for those financially impacted by AI.

stories.headline: Canada introduces Bill C-34 to bar under-16s from social media and regulate AI chatbots

key_facts.fact: On June 10, Culture Minister Marc Miller tabled Bill C-34 (Safe Social Media Act) in the House of Commons, enacting the Digital Safety Act and creating a new Digital Safety Commission of Canada to enforce it.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 10, 2026, the Government of Canada introduced Bill C-34, the Safe Social Media Act, which would enact two new Acts: The Digital Safety Act and the Digital Safety Commission of Canada Act.

key_facts.fact: The bill imposes a 16-year-old minimum age for social media accounts, with a possible exemption pathway if a service can demonstrate sufficient safeguards for children; existing under-16 accounts would be deactivated.
key_facts.excerpt: The law bars those under 16 from creating a new account on platforms like Instagram, Facebook and TikTok. It also deactivated existing ones.

key_facts.fact: The legislation also regulates AI chatbot services, requiring crisis-intervention protocols for self-harm, suicide and violence, and obligations to mitigate harmful content for children.
key_facts.excerpt: Bill C-34, introduced Wednesday in the House of Commons, would also regulate the companies behind AI chatbots by imposing on them a duty to act responsibly. That includes measures to lower the risk of chatbots communicating harmful content and putting in place crisis intervention protocols for cases involving self-harm, suicide or violence.

key_facts.fact: Maximum penalties for violations are the greater of C$10M (about US$7M) or 3% of gross global revenue.
key_facts.excerpt: The maximum penalty for a violation is the greater of $10m ($7m; £5m), or 3% of gross global revenue.

key_facts.fact: Platforms will be required to remove content that sexually victimizes a child or revictimizes a survivor, and non-consensual intimate images, within 24 hours; seven categories of harmful content are covered in total.
key_facts.excerpt: The bill covers seven types of harmful content, including content that induces a child to harm themselves, content that incites violence and foments hatred and non-consensual intimate content. Social media platforms will have to remove two types of content within 24 hours -- content that sexually victimizes a child or revictimizes a survivor and non-consensual intimate images.

stories.headline: Google open-sources DiffusionGemma, a 26B text-diffusion model that generates 4x faster

key_facts.fact: Google released DiffusionGemma, an experimental open Mixture-of-Experts model that uses text diffusion to generate entire blocks of text in parallel instead of token by token.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we're introducing DiffusionGemma, an experimental open model that explores text diffusion, an exceptionally fast approach to text generation. Released under an Apache 2.0 license, this 26B Mixture of Experts (MoE) model moves beyond the sequential token-by-token processing of typical autoregressive Large Language Models (LLMs). Instead, it generates entire blocks of text simultaneously, delivering up to 4x faster text generation on GPUs.

key_facts.fact: The model has 26 billion total parameters but activates only 3.8 billion per inference, and fits in 18GB of VRAM when quantized — running on a single RTX 5090 consumer GPU.
key_facts.excerpt: Operating as a 26B total Mixture of Experts (MoE) model that activates only 3.8B parameters during inference, DiffusionGemma fits comfortably within 18GB VRAM limits of high-end dedicated consumer GPUs when quantized.

key_facts.fact: DiffusionGemma reaches 1000+ tokens per second on a single NVIDIA H100 and 700+ tokens per second on an RTX 5090.
key_facts.excerpt: By shifting the decode bottleneck from memory-bandwidth to compute, DiffusionGemma generates up to 4x faster token output on dedicated GPUs. (1000+ tokens per second on a single NVIDIA H100, 700+ tokens per second on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090).

key_facts.fact: The weights are on Hugging Face under an Apache 2.0 license and the model is the first diffusion LLM natively supported in vLLM.
key_facts.excerpt: Download the Weights: Access the weights of the experimental model(released under the Apache 2.0 license) directly on Hugging Face. Use Your Favorite Inference Frameworks: Run the model efficiently using vLLM, Hugging Face Transformers, and MLX.

key_facts.fact: On benchmarks DiffusionGemma underperforms the same-size autoregressive Gemma 4 26B A4B, a trade-off Google explicitly accepts for speed-critical use cases.
key_facts.excerpt: The experimental model trails standard Gemma 4 on every benchmark, a tradeoff Google says is worth it for tasks like code infilling and in-line editing. For applications that demand maximum quality, we recommend deploying standard Gemma 4.

key_facts.fact: DiffusionGemma denoises 256-token blocks in parallel using bidirectional attention, designed for inline editing, code infilling, and other interactive local workflows.
key_facts.excerpt: To facilitate text diffusion, the search giant replaced the latter model's attention mechanism, the software module it uses to interpret prompts. The original mechanism inferred the meaning of each word in a prompt by analyzing the preceding text. The new attention module also reviews the text that follows a given word.

stories.headline: Microsoft blocks Claude Fable 5 in internal Copilot over Anthropic's 30-day data retention

key_facts.fact: Microsoft has restricted employees from using Claude Fable 5 in internal GitHub Copilot because Anthropic's new data retention rules conflict with Microsoft's compliance posture.
key_facts.excerpt: While Microsoft quickly rolled out Claude Fable 5 to its GitHub Copilot and Foundry customers, I'm told the model isn't available in the model picker that Microsoft employees use for internal versions of GitHub Copilot. All other Claude models are still available internally at Microsoft, because they operate under Zero Data Retention (ZDR) rules.

key_facts.fact: Fable 5 requires Anthropic to retain prompts and outputs for 30 days to operate its new safety classifiers, with flagged content stored up to two years.
key_facts.excerpt: Claude Fable 5 requires data retention to operate Anthropic's new safety classifiers, meaning Anthropic retains prompts and outputs and deletes this data after 30 days. Some prompts and outputs can even be stored for up to two years if they're flagged as violating Anthropic's usage policy.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft's legal team is evaluating the policy and has not committed to a timeline for approving Fable 5 internally; concerns center on customer data and confidential information.
key_facts.excerpt: For Microsoft, which handles sensitive customer data and proprietary code, the retention window raises compliance and confidentiality concerns. The company has told employees that its lawyers are evaluating whether these requirements align with Microsoft's own standards for data protection.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic has said the retention policy applies on first- and third-party surfaces, and that retained data will not be used to train new Claude models or for purposes unrelated to safety.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has said the new 30-day retention policy applies to both first- and third-party surfaces, adding that it will ensure data deletion after 30 days in almost all cases, and that it will not use this data to train new Claude models or for any purpose unrelated to safety.

key_facts.fact: For external GitHub Copilot customers, Fable 5 is opt-in and disabled by default, so enterprise admins must explicitly enable it.
key_facts.excerpt: Fable 5 is the only model in Copilot's Claude lineup that breaks Zero Data Retention because Anthropic's safety classifiers require retaining prompts and outputs for up to 30 days and flagged items for up to two years. For external GitHub Copilot customers, the policy is opt-in and disabled by default; enterprise admins must explicitly enable it.

stories.headline: Nvidia halves SOCAMM capacity in Vera Rubin Superchip module amid LPDDR5X memory shortage

key_facts.fact: TrendForce reported on June 10 that Nvidia has decided to halve the SOCAMM capacity for its next-generation Vera Rubin Superchip module to address anticipated LPDDR5X memory supply shortages by early 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: On June 10, 2026, TrendForce reported that NVIDIA NVDA has decided to halve the SOCAMM capacity for its next-generation Vera Rubin Superchip module. This decision comes in response to anticipated supply shortages expected by early 2027, rather than a revision of total memory demand.

key_facts.fact: Rather than reducing total memory demand, Nvidia is cutting single-chip capacity while raising module shipments — a tactic aimed at preserving market share as LPDDR5X supply tightens.
key_facts.excerpt: By reducing single-chip capacity while increasing module shipments, NVIDIA aims to strengthen its market share amid a growing demand for LPDDR5X memory, which cannot currently be met.

key_facts.fact: Vera Rubin is Nvidia's next-generation Superchip platform; the first gigawatt of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems is targeted for the second half of 2026 under its 10GW-plus letter of intent with OpenAI.
key_facts.excerpt: In September 2025, Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent for at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia committing up to $100 billion in OpenAI as capacity comes online. The first gigawatt was targeted for the second half of 2026 using Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform.

key_facts.excerpt: Sources: Sam Altman told staff that OpenAI is expected to go public 'within the next year' and OpenAI plans a tender offer 'very soon' at a $687.69 share price.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is preparing an employee tender 'very soon' at a $687.69 per-share price.

stories.headline: OpenAI weighs drastic token price cuts to head off an Anthropic price war

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is considering drastically lowering its prices for tokens, the central unit for measuring AI inference costs, according to the Wall Street Journal.
key_facts.excerpt: Sources: OpenAI is considering drastically lowering its price for tokens in anticipation of similar cuts the company expects at Anthropic. The company might lower prices for tokens, the central unit for gauging AI costs, though the discussions are still in flux.

key_facts.fact: The discussions are framed internally as preparation for cuts OpenAI expects Anthropic to make, with both sides chasing developer and enterprise share.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI Considers Drastic Price Cuts, Anticipating War for Users With Anthropic. The company might lower prices for tokens, the central unit for gauging AI costs, though the discussions are still in flux.

key_facts.fact: Markets read the report as a threat to margins and to OpenAI's profitability ahead of a potential IPO.
key_facts.excerpt: *OpenAI Price Cuts Could Threaten Margins, Profits Ahead of Potential IPO, Sources Say — WSJ maybe should have rushed that IPO out while nobody was checking their token bills.

stories.headline: Opendoor shuts India operations, lays off ~250 staff to rebuild with US AI-native teams

key_facts.fact: On June 10, Opendoor CEO Kaz Nejatian told staff the company is winding down its India operations, affecting nearly 250 employees across offices in Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad opened in 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Opendoor itself had built a large team in India to handle manual workflows across fragmented systems, Nejatian said. The company had nearly 250 employees in India when it opened offices in Chennai and Bengaluru in 2024.

key_facts.fact: Nejatian said the team handled manual workflows across fragmented systems, and that those processes have been unified and handed to 'small AI-native customer-facing teams' in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: 'As we've unified these systems and have hired small AI-native customer-facing teams throughout the US, we need all this operational work to be done in person and close to our customers,' the company said in its note.

key_facts.fact: Opendoor's global headcount fell to 1,042 at end-2025 from 1,470 a year earlier; non-US headcount dropped to 184 from 342 over the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: Securities filings show Opendoor employed 1,042 people globally at the end of last year, compared with 1,470 a year earlier. Similarly, its non-U.S. workforce declined to 184 employees at the end of last year, compared with 342 employees at the end of 2024.

key_facts.fact: Investors and outsourcing analysts called the move 'a watershed moment in AI Ops', viewing it as an early example of AI altering the economics that made India a global hub for back-office work.
key_facts.excerpt: Investors and commentators labelled it 'a watershed moment in AI Ops'... Keshav Lohia, a venture capitalist at Emergent Ventures, said that the outsourcing... 'shows how advancements in frontier models are...'

key_facts.fact: Affected staff receive severance, outplacement services and other transition support; a small subset will remain temporarily to complete the transition of key workstreams.
key_facts.excerpt: The company said affected employees will receive transition support, including severance packages, outplacement services and other resources. A small number of staff members will remain temporarily to assist with the transition of key workstreams.

stories.headline: Oracle plans $40B FY27 raise and ~$70B capex as RPO hits $638B; stock falls ~10% on capex shock

key_facts.fact: Oracle reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $19.2 billion, up 21% year-over-year, ahead of the $19.1B Street estimate; adjusted EPS of $2.11 beat the $1.97 estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: Oracle reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $19.2 billion, up 21% year on year, and adjusted earnings of $2.11 per share, beating analyst estimates of $19.1 billion and $1.97 respectively.

key_facts.fact: Remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion, up from $553 billion three months earlier and well above the $589.5B analyst estimate; four customers each signed deals worth more than $8 billion in the quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: Remaining performance obligations, Oracle's measure of contracted future revenue, reached $638 billion at the end of the quarter, up from $553 billion three months earlier and well above the $589.5 billion analysts expected. The company said most of the new bookings were for large-scale AI contracts in which customers prepaid for expensive GPU servers.

key_facts.fact: Oracle spent roughly $55.7 billion on capex in fiscal 2026 (vs. its own $50B guidance) and expects net cash capex of about $70 billion in FY27, with reported capex $20B–$25B higher due to customer prepayments and timing.
key_facts.excerpt: The company spent approximately $55.7 billion on capital expenditure in the fiscal year ended May 31, exceeding its previous guidance of $50 billion. Oracle now expects to spend roughly $70 billion in net capital expenditure in fiscal 2027, with the reported figure $20 billion to $25 billion higher due to prepayments for components, CFO Hilary Maxson said on the earnings call.

key_facts.fact: Oracle plans to raise about $40 billion through debt and equity in fiscal 2027 — including a previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance — after raising $43B in debt and $5B in equity in FY26; it does not expect to issue additional debt in calendar 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: In fiscal year 2026, Oracle raised $43 billion in debt financing and $5 billion in equity financing. In fiscal year 2027, Oracle expects to raise approximately $40 billion through a combination of debt and equity financing including its previously announced $20 billion at-the-market equity issuance. Oracle does not expect to issue additional debt in calendar year 2026.

key_facts.fact: Prepaid and customer-supplied GPU portions of Oracle's large AI contracts now total $75 billion, which Oracle says 'substantially reduces' the capital it needs to raise for its AI data center build-out.
key_facts.excerpt: Most of the RPO increase in both Q3 and Q4 were large scale AI contracts where the customer prepaid Oracle for the purchase of the GPUs, or the customer bought and supplied the GPUs to Oracle. The prepaid and customer supplied hardware portions of our large AI contracts now total $75 billion.

key_facts.fact: ORCL stock dropped about 10% in extended trading on the FY27 capex and capital-raise outlook; co-CEO Clay Magouyrk said Oracle is bringing nearly 1 gigawatt of computing online in the current quarter, roughly matching all of fiscal 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The stock dropped 10% in extended trading as the company plans to raise more money to finance its AI buildout. [...] The company is looking to bring online almost one gigawatt worth of computing power in the current quarter, roughly the total for fiscal 2026, Oracle CEO Clay Magouyrk said on a conference call with analysts.

stories.headline: Ricursive, founded by Google AlphaChip leads, raises $335M to build an end-to-end AI chip design model

key_facts.fact: Palo Alto startup Ricursive, founded by the two leads of Google's AlphaChip project, has raised $335 million to develop an end-to-end AI model for chip design.
key_facts.excerpt: Palo Alto, Calif. — Startup Ricursive, founded by the two leads from Google's famous AlphaChip project, is aiming to develop an end-to-end AI model for chip design. The new AI frontier lab is focused on hardware workload co-optimization, with the first stages of its rollout targeting workload-specific chip design for third parties. The company has raised $335 million, which will largely be spent on GPU compute hours as it trains and tests its model.

key_facts.fact: Most of the capital will be spent on GPU compute hours to train and test the model.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has raised $335 million, which will largely be spent on GPU compute hours as it trains and tests its model.

key_facts.fact: Ricursive is rolling out in three phases: starting with workload-specific chip design services for third parties, then an end-to-end model that ingests workloads and outputs GDSII files ready for manufacturing.
key_facts.excerpt: Ricursive has planned three stages for its technology rollout. The company is currently working on phase one. In this phase, Ricursive will take on portions of chip design for chip companies, improving performance and helping companies get to market faster. Phase two will combine the stages of chip design into an end-to-end model that can ingest workloads and spit out GDSII files ready for manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: The startup trains on generally available web data and open-source chip data and can generate synthetic data; co-founder Anna Goldie argued advanced models need less data because knowledge can transfer across tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Ricursive is training its model on generally available web data and open-source chip data, but can also create and use synthetic data to avoid hitting the limits of what is available in the real world today. Advanced AI models need less data, Goldie said, since knowledge can transfer across tasks.

stories.headline: Texas Governor Abbott directs PUC and ERCOT to make data centers pay for their grid costs

key_facts.fact: Governor Greg Abbott sent a letter on June 10 directing the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and ERCOT to require data centers to fund their own electric infrastructure so residential ratepayers do not absorb those costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Abbott's letter uses stronger language, directing the agency to 'take action to require data centers to pay for all of their electric infrastructure costs to ensure that no residential ratepayer is burdened by those costs.'

key_facts.fact: Abbott ordered the agencies to submit a memorandum by July 17 outlining actions to protect ratepayers and required the PUC to initiate action to reduce residential transmission costs by July 31.
key_facts.excerpt: Submit a memo to Abbott by July 17 with actions they can take to protect residential and small business ratepayers. For PUC, 'initiate action' to reduce residential customers' infrastructure costs by July 31.

key_facts.fact: More than 480 'large' data centers have applied to connect to the ERCOT grid through 2032; only about a dozen of those currently drawing power are classified as large users (consuming at least as much as 18,750 households).
key_facts.excerpt: More than 480 'large' data centers have requested to connect to the ERCOT grid through 2032, according to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, the grid operator. Currently, only a dozen of the hundreds of data centers drawing power from the state's primary grid are considered 'large' electricity users, meaning they consume at least as much power as 18,750 households.

key_facts.fact: Abbott also pledged 2027 legislative priorities: codifying the cost-payment rule, requiring water-efficient cooling, mandating annual electricity and water reporting, repealing data center sales tax exemptions, and adding noise protections for neighbors.
key_facts.excerpt: The governor said he plans to 'codify' the PUCT's actions to force data centers to pay for their own electric infrastructure and contribute to the state's electric supply. Abbott also said he will work to pass legislation that will require data centers to use 'water-efficient technologies' and report their electricity and water usage; repeal financial incentives and tax exemptions for these facilities; and reduce their impact on nearby communities.

key_facts.fact: The move marks the first time the Republican governor has sought to put limits on data center growth, which has drawn backlash even in heavily GOP areas; the Texas Senate Committee on Finance will meet July 27 to discuss the sales tax exemption.
key_facts.excerpt: The Texas Senate Committee on Finance will meet July 27 at 10:30am to discuss the sales tax exemption for data centers.

stories.headline: Ukraine drones hit Afipsky oil refinery as Russia launches 221-drone overnight barrage

key_facts.fact: From the evening of June 10 into the morning of June 11, Russia attacked Ukraine with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles from Belgorod and 221 strike UAVs (Shahed, Gerbera, Italmas and Parodia decoys), launched from Orel, Kursk, Bryansk, Primorsko-Akhtarsk and occupied Crimea.
key_facts.excerpt: the enemy attacked Ukraine with two Iskander-M ballistic missiles launched from Russia's Belgorod region, as well as 221 attack drones, including Shahed drones (including jet-powered variants), Gerbera, Italmas, and Parodiya decoy drones.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's air force reported it shot down or suppressed 195 of the 221 enemy targets, while ballistic missiles and 21 strike drones hit nine locations and falling debris was recorded at eight more.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian defense forces neutralized 195 of 221 enemy targets overnight into Thursday, though ballistic missiles and 21 strike drones hit 9 locations... Ballistic missiles and 21 strike drones were recorded as hitting 9 locations, with downed drone debris falling at 8 locations.

key_facts.fact: Drone debris triggered a fire at the Afipsky Oil Refinery in Krasnodar Krai, one of Russia's largest refineries; three civilians were injured in Krasnodar and Russia's MoD said air defenses intercepted 330 Ukrainian drones across multiple regions overnight.
key_facts.excerpt: A fire broke out at one of Russia's largest oil refineries overnight after what local authorities said was a Ukrainian drone attack... According to the Russian Ministry of Defense, air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 330 Ukrainian drones over Russian territory overnight.

key_facts.fact: Russia imposed flight restrictions on the evening of June 10 at airports in Tambov (Donskoye), Krasnodar (Pashkovsky), Sochi, Gelendzhik and Zhukovsky near Moscow due to the drone threat.
key_facts.excerpt: Due to the drone threat, Rosaviatsiya imposed restrictions on airport operations in Tambov (Donskoye), Krasnodar (Pashkovsky), Sochi, Gelendzhik, and Zhukovsky in the Moscow region starting on the evening of June 10.

stories.headline: US and Iran trade fresh strikes; Iran hits bases in Bahrain, Kuwait and Jordan

key_facts.fact: US Central Command launched 'self-defense strikes' on Iranian air defenses, ground control stations and radar sites near the Strait of Hormuz on June 10, 2026, in retaliation for the downing of a US Army AH-64 Apache helicopter the prior day.
key_facts.excerpt: The immediate catalyst was a US Central Command operation targeting Iranian air defenses, ground control stations, and radar sites near the Strait of Hormuz. The military stated the strikes were retaliation for the downing of an American Apache helicopter.

key_facts.fact: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it launched drone attacks on the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain and the Ali Al Salem airbase in Kuwait, plus a long-range missile strike on an airbase in Azraq, Jordan, claiming it struck 21 US targets including an F-35 hangar.
key_facts.excerpt: In a statement carried by Iran's state media on Wednesday, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it launched drone attacks on the US Fifth Fleet in Bahrain and the Ali Al Salem airbase in Kuwait, as well as a long-range missile strike on an airbase in Azraq, Jordan. It said it attacked 21 US targets and destroyed four of them, including an F-35 fighter jet hangar at the base in Jordan.

key_facts.fact: Iran announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz 'until further notice' and said it hit two 'violating ships' trying to transit, while US CENTCOM denied the strait was closed and said commercial traffic was rising.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran says Strait of Hormuz completely closed 'until further notice' ... CentCom denies closure of Hormuz ... US Energy Secretary Wright said vessel traffic in the Gulf and oil exports through the Strait are rising despite ongoing disruptions.

key_facts.fact: President Trump said Iran was 'playing us for suckers' and warned the US would attack 'very hard' if a deal was not finalized, accusing Tehran of stalling negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: 'We're going to be attacking them – attacking them very hard,' Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. 'We were really close to a deal, but they keep tapping us along, they keep playing us for suckers.'

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose more than 2% to about $94/barrel and WTI reached $91.46 by midday June 10 as traders absorbed the strikes; US crude inventories fell 7.228 million barrels last week, the seventh straight weekly draw.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent extended gains and rose more than 2% to $93 a barrel on Wednesday as traders weighed escalating tensions in the Middle East... EIA data showed US crude inventories fell by 7.228 million barrels last week, a seventh consecutive weekly decline.

key_facts.fact: OPEC oil production fell to roughly 16.13 million barrels per day in May 2026, the lowest in more than two decades, driven mainly by a US naval blockade on Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz; OPEC+ still agreed on June 7 to a further 188,000 bpd output hike from July.
key_facts.excerpt: OPEC crude output fell 1.06 million barrels per day month-on-month in May, dropping to the lowest level in over two decades. The decline was driven mainly by a U.S. naval blockade on Iran and disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz.
